entrypoint.invocation: python -m ao_kernel (wheel-installed venv, outside source checkout)

notes: scripts/packaging_smoke.py is extended (additive _smoke_repo_intelligence_cli function) to drive `python -m ao_kernel repo scan|index|query` against a throwaway project using the wheel-installed venv Python, from an outside-source-checkout cwd. The full flow remains: build sdist+wheel, fresh venv, install wheel only, run all CLI entry points, run demo_review.py --cleanup, then drive RI-7.4 scan/index/query scenarios.
Each scenario asserts the documented exit code + stderr contract; the script raises SystemExit on contract violation so CI fails closed.

The script writes a per-run JSON evidence artifact to build/packaging-smoke/ri7-packaging-smoke-evidence.v1.json that validates against ao_kernel/defaults/schemas/ri7-scan-index-query-packaging-smoke-evidence.schema.v1.json.

A supplementary in-process subprocess test (tests/test_ri7_scan_index_query_packaging_smoke.py) pins the same six scenarios using the current pytest interpreter; this layer is documented as supplementary and does not replace the wheel-installed evidence.

Fail-closed scenarios run in a deterministic minimal env: only PATH/HOME/TMPDIR/lang/Windows-SYSTEMROOT inherited from the host, every known provider/embedding env (OPENAI_API_KEY, AO_KERNEL_OPENAI_API_KEY, AO_KERNEL_EMBEDDING_API_KEY/PROVIDER/MODEL/BASE_URL, GOOGLE_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, XAI_API_KEY, QWEN_API_KEY) explicitly scrubbed, then AO_KERNEL_VECTOR_BACKEND is set to disabled (or inmemory for the API-key path) and a dummy OPENAI_API_KEY is set for the backend-isolation scenarios (both repo_index_write_vectors_fails_closed_without_backend and repo_query_fails_closed_without_manifest_or_backend) so the CLI reaches and rejects on the backend / prerequisite-missing branch. Query scenarios assert on the CLI's documented prerequisite-missing contract (manifest-missing or backend-missing or API-key-missing) because the CLI checks the vector index manifest first; the smoke does not over-claim that a single specific branch is reached.

No support widening. No production platform claim. No live adapter execution. No public SDK signature change. No MCP exposure. No context-compiler auto-feed. No workflow or branch protection mutation.
